youtube.title: In 1940, the King Wanted Halifax as Prime Minister, Not Churchill #Shorts
youtube.description:
On 9 May 1940, Chamberlain and the King both wanted Lord Halifax to be prime minister. Halifax said no. Two weeks later, at Dunkirk, he argued for finding out what peace terms Britain could get. The War Cabinet sided with Churchill. UNHISTORY asks: what if Halifax had said yes?

Photos: Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe (public domain); Cecil Beaton / IWM MH 26392 and IWM HU 1137 (Crown copyright expired).

Full episode: https://youtu.be/MlVCM0_2xaY

youtube.title: The SS Arrest List for Britain Had Churchill on It #Shorts
youtube.description:
In 1940 the SS drew up a handbook for the invasion of Britain. At the back, the Sonderfahndungsliste G.B.: about 2,800 people to be arrested. Entry 49 is Winston Churchill. This is page 32 of the Imperial War Museum's copy.

Document photo: Black Book pages 32-33, IWM copy (public domain). Map: Natural Earth (public domain).

youtube.title: Hitler's Arch Was Tested on This Concrete Block. The Ground Failed. #Shorts
youtube.description:
Hitler wanted Berlin rebuilt as Germania by 1950, with a triumphal arch more than 100 metres tall. In 1941 engineers poured a block of about 12,500 tonnes of concrete to test the ground. It sank about three times the 6 cm limit. It is still standing in Berlin.
